entries.title: Proverbs 26:1
segments: ¶As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour beseemeth not a fool.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
segments: ¶As the sparrow for flitting about, as the swallow for flying, so a curse undeserved shall not come.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:3
segments: ¶A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the back of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4
segments: ¶Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:5
segments: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
segments: ¶He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off [his own] feet, [and] drinketh damage.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
segments: The legs of the lame hang loose; so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
segments: As a bag of gems in a stoneheap, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
segments: [As] a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
segments: ¶A master roughly worketh every one: he both hireth the fool and hireth passers-by.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:11
segments: ¶As a dog turneth back to its vomit, [so] a fool repeateth his folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:12
segments: ¶Hast thou seen a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope of a fool than of him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:13
segments: ¶The sluggard saith, There is a fierce lion in the way; a lion is in the midst of the streets!

entries.title: Proverbs 26:14
segments: ¶[As] the door turneth upon its hinges, so the sluggard upon his bed.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:15
segments: ¶The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish: it wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
segments: ¶A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven [men] that answer discreetly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
segments: ¶He that passing by vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, is [like] one that taketh a dog by the ears.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:18
segments: ¶As a madman who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,

entries.title: Proverbs 26:19
segments: so is a man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am I not in sport?

entries.title: Proverbs 26:20
segments: ¶Where no wood is, the fire goeth out; and where there is no talebearer, the contention ceaseth.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:21
segments: [As] coals for hot coals, and wood for fire, so is a contentious man to inflame strife.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:22
segments: The words of a talebearer are as dainty morsels, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
segments: ¶Ardent lips, and a wicked heart, are [as] an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:24
segments: ¶He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, but he layeth up deceit within him:

entries.title: Proverbs 26:25
segments: when his voice is gracious, believe him not, for there are seven abominations in his heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:26
segments: Though [his] hatred is covered by dissimulation, his wickedness shall be made manifest in the congregation.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:27
segments: ¶Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:28
segments: ¶A lying tongue hateth those that are injured by it, and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
